invariant: Java computes a flat state diagram's SVEK body envelope by drawing the same clusters, nodes, and solved edges used for final output through LimitFinder. The union includes each primitive's painter semantics: UEmpty contributes its complete rectangle; URectangle starts one pixel above and left and ends one pixel inside plus shadow; UEllipse ends one pixel inside plus shadow; ULine contributes both endpoints; DotPath contributes every cubic endpoint and control point after shaft retraction; UPolygon contributes polygon extrema plus ten horizontal pixels on each side; and UText contributes its measured box from baseline-height+1.5 through baseline+1.5. SvekResult then translates every node, edge, and cluster by (6-minX, 6-minY) and reports the painted span plus 15 pixels. SvekEdge.appendTable's fixed HTML label marker constrains Graphviz layout, including self-loop clearance, but SvekResult.drawU paints the solved edge's path, decoration, and original label block rather than that marker. The marker's layout-only extent must therefore never enlarge the exported painted envelope. At the file boundary, CucaDiagram.getDefaultMargins adds its backward-compatible 5-pixel right and bottom margins. SvgGraphics.ensureVisible then integerizes that final positive dimension exactly once as (int)(dimension+1), equivalent to ceil(dimension) except that an already integral dimension gains one. Rust must therefore apply Java's integerization to painted-span-plus-20, not add one to the floating dimension and ceil it again. The minimum visible painter sits at coordinate 6. Arrowhead polygons remain at the unretracted contact tip while the shaft is shortened by the decoration length, and the complete solved label block participates in the same envelope. Width, height, and origin are therefore one consequence of the emitted primitives and named export decorators, not independent Graphviz layout dimensions or node-rank heuristics.
causal_divergence: The original Rust flat state path reconstructed the envelope in several disconnected passes. Implementation 1b75e728 introduced a single primitive-aware collector, and implementation 3538e6c4 subsequently supplied exact transition-to-EdgePath identity. The collector already knows how to measure a self-loop from its retracted spline, arrowhead, and emitted label block, but its activation gate rejects every diagram containing a self transition. Those diagrams fall back to the legacy maximum pass, whose mixed-label branch unconditionally includes LayoutResult.width. For a wide fixed self-loop label marker, that Graphviz layout width extends beyond every painter emitted by SvekResult.drawU. The preserved review_self_loop_reversed_lazy_matrix counterexample consequently has byte-identical Java and Rust nodes, paths, polygons, and text, yet Rust advertises an 847px canvas instead of Java's 810px. This isolates the remaining divergence to the activation gate and layout-only marker leakage, not route identity, branch count, or a new geometry constant. The route review's four-lane and compound-endpoint failures remain separate counterexamples and are not claimed by this correction.

Measure each self-link from the exact retracted path, arrowhead polygon, and emitted label block already shared with final emission; continue using its enlarged Graphviz label size only to solve layout.
